messages:
morgan: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a quick checkin about an idea to coalesce small tenant envelopes at the ingest layer to reduce per-envelope overhead and request churn. thinking tradeoffs: cost savings vs accuracy of per-tenant metrics/billing and late enrichment.

ravi: +1 on exploring. can you sketch the high-level flow you have in mind?

morgan: idea: when envelopes under N bytes or <X events/sec for a tenant arrive, we buffer for up to T ms and merge into a single envelope with metadata pointing to the tenants included. keep the original event list (no aggregation) so downstream can still attribute.

alisa: hmm — merging multiple tenants into one envelope will break a lot of assumptions in the enrichment stage (we expect 1 tenant per envelope). we either need a small decoder change or a pre-split step.

morgan: yes. plan A: make enrichment accept multi-tenant envelope (iterate inner items). Plan B: split at the gateway before enrichment but after coalescing for transport savings. Plan A reduces copies.

sam: latency SLO concern: buffering up to T ms — what T are you thinking? 50ms? 200ms? at 200ms we might blow some tail-latency budgets for real-time traces.

morgan: thinking 25-100ms window depending on tenant class. default 50ms for low-priority tenants, 0ms for high-priority (no coalescing).

nina: how does this interact with sampling and billing? if we merge, do we risk over/under attributing token costs when we later drop sampled items?
ravi: good point. we'd need to tag each inner item with original sampling/billing key and any pre-sampling decision. coalescing itself must be orthogonal to sampling.

ops-bot: deploy checklist triggered: "coalesce-prototype" feature flag required, metrics prefixed with coalesce.*, add canary to us-west2.

alisa: also operationally, querying by tenant across coalesced envelopes might increase query complexity. we should ensure query engine can quickly index inner tenant ids without exploding cardinality. maybe keep a flattened top-level index for billing keys.
sam: could we maintain a separate lightweight envelope index mapping envelope_id -> tenant_ids for fast lookup? small cache evict after retention window.
morgan: yes, that was Plan C: emit a tiny admission record to the metadata store: {envelope_id, tenant_ids, ingest_ts, size}. keeps main payload compact and avoids unpack at query time.

ravi: curious about memory/CPU tradeoffs vs network savings. coalescing reduces number of records downstream but increases CPU to merge/unmerge. do we have rough numbers?
morgan: rough microbench: merging 10 tiny envelopes (~1KB each) into one adds ~0.5ms CPU and saves ~6KB on network + N TCP headers; at scale that looks ~20-30% reduction in per-enveloping bandwidth for trace-heavy tenants. numbers vary across proto.

nina: plus we need to ensure encryption/KMS semantics hold. if customers require per-tenant envelope keys, merging might break HSM expectations.
morgan: flagged — will add KMS constraint: only allowed when tenant key-policy == shared-ingest-key, else skip coalesce.

dev-bot: note saved to design note: /docs/ingest/coalesce-proposal.md (draft).

alisa: next steps that seem reasonable: 1) prototype coalescer as a feature-flagged module in edge-proxy, 2) add admission record emitter, 3) adjust enrichment to accept multi-item envelopes or implement fast-split, 4) run canary in low-traffic region for 48h.
sam: add test scenarios: tail-latency under 99.9, sampling+late-enrich, per-tenant billing reconciliation with missing items, KMS-policy skips.
morgan: i'll draft a lightweight RFC with the microbench numbers and canary plan. tagging @ravi @alisa for review.

ravi: thanks — ping when RFC is up.

nina: +1. also please include a section on observability: coalesce.* metrics, admission-record success/failure, per-tenant delta checks so we can detect lost attribution early.
morgan: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
